description: This is a false-colour satellite or aerial image depicting a landscape mosaic of various land cover types. The image primarily uses a colour composite where dense, actively vegetated areas (likely forests or dense scrub) appear dark reddish-brown on the left and right edges. A large central area is labelled "Natural grassland" and appears in lighter pinkish-grey tones, encompassing a dark, irregularly shaped water body in its upper-central part. Two distinct areas labelled "Heathland" are visible: one in the mid-left and another in the upper-right, both characterized by darker reddish-brown to maroon hues, often bordering the lighter grassland. In the lower-right section, an area is labelled "Sparsely vegetated" and exhibits lighter greenish-blue tones, suggesting exposed soil or very low-density vegetation. The landscape is crisscrossed by thin, bright linear features, likely roads or tracks. Smaller, darker water bodies are also scattered throughout the lower-central part of the image. The imagery highlights the visual distinction between these land cover types, useful for classification in environmental monitoring programmes like Copernicus Land Monitoring Service (CLMS).
